thread:
andrew: incident-bot just fired for metrics-pipeline - prometheus_scrape_failure on prod (multiple targets). PagerDuty also paged the metrics oncall. Anyone seeing this? :rotating_light:

incident-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: SERVICE=metrics-pipeline | ALERT=prometheus_scrape_failure | SEVERITY=high | fired at 2025-11-03T14:06:05Z

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident #INC12345 created and notified oncall. Escalation policy: metrics-oncall -> eng-sre-team.

sara: seeing a cascade of scrape failures from exporters in eu-west1. Scrapes time out, status 504 in the metadata logs. Dashboards are showing "no data" for request_per_min metrics.

mike: confirmed. Also seeing kafka consumer lag grow for metrics-ingest by ~40k. Likely backlog because scrapes stalled.

andrew: can we confirm root cause quickly? Is it network flake to the exporter fleet or Prometheus hitting thundering herd?

emma: initial quick check: prometheus scrape queue is full, scrape_concurrency at 20. Many targets are returning 502/timeout. Example from prom logs:

```
level=error ts=2025-11-03T14:05:59.123Z component=scrape target="node-exporter:9100" err="context deadline exceeded (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)"
```

emma: looks like the exporter side (node-exporter / app-exporter) is slow in eu-west1. Could be overload or transient GC.

andrew: ok, plan: 1) ack PD incident and annotate 2) try to reduce scrape_concurrency to throttle Prom and protect exporters 3) if backlog continues, spin up a temporary scrape proxy / fallback metric mirror 4) notify product / ops if customer-facing dashboards impacted.

oncall-ops: acked oncall. I'm taking lead. Reducing scrape_concurrency now to 10.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC12345 acked by oncall-ops at 2025-11-03T14:08:10Z.

mike: lowering concurrency already showing reduced error rate on some targets. But kafka lag still climbing; ingestion pipeline has to catch up.

andrew: can you run a quick grep for exporters with high cpu or OOMs? Might be a rollout gone wrong.

emma: checked node-exporter pods in eu-west1: cpu spiking on a subset (aws autoscaled nodes) and a recent config push to exporters 10:45 UTC changed scrape_timeout globally from 10s->15s — might have had unintended side effects on connection handling. I'm opening a quick PR rollback to revert exporter config.

sara: also noticed an unusual spike in metric cardinality for request.latency.histogram in app-exporter. Could be a bad client generating high-cardinality labels. That would amplify scrape cost.

andrew: good catch. If cardinality spiked, exporters may be blowing memory and slowing scrapes. Work through steps: revert exporter config, whitelist critical metrics, restart a subset of exporter pods with lower memory pressure, monitor.

oncall-ops: rolling restart of eu-west1 exporter deployment in 3 batches to avoid total outage. First batch restarted at 14:12Z.

emma: also adding a temporary scrape_timeout override to 8s for the noisy targets so Prom doesn't hang waiting. Patching now.

(1 minute later)

mike: kafka consumer lag stopped growing after first batch; ingestion throughput recovering. Prom errors reduced from ~300/sec to ~25/sec.

andrew: great. start drafting customer-impact note: affected dashboards in product-analytics and infra-health. Potentially customers using real-time dashboards might have seen stale/no-data for ~8-12 minutes. No request failures to API layer — only metrics visibility degraded.

sara: agreeing: severity assessment = high for internal observability, medium for customer impact. No SLA breach to report right now.

incident-bot: oncall handoff due in 45 minutes. If this stays stable, we'll close the incident.

andrew: leave one person on watch to monitor kafka lag and scrapes, otherwise handoff at 15:00Z. I'll update the PD incident with mitigations and timeline.

pagerduty-bot: INC12345 annotated: mitigations applied: decreased scrape_concurrency, restart exporter deployment (eu-west1), revert exporter config change, temporary timeout overrides.

mike: confirming all eu-west1 exporter pods back to Ready=1/1. Prometheus scrape failures trending down to normal.

emma: running a sweep for high-cardinality series: found a client that introduced unbounded label sets. I've created an alert rule to block new label cardinality > 200 for that metric and sent a note to the app team.

andrew: good. next steps: 1) root cause postmortem draft (include config change + cardinality spike) 2) make exporter config changes gated behind canary + mem/cpu autoscaling 3) add circuit-breaker in Prom prometheus exporter manager to avoid full queue saturation 4) update runbook with steps we executed.

sara: I'll start the postmortem draft and tag the app team. Will assign action items.

oncall-ops: leaving watch on channel for 30m. If no regressions, I'll close PD in 45m and mark as resolved.

andrew: thanks team. Quick note for ops: when resolving, include timeline and the customer-impact blurb.

(30 minutes later)

oncall-ops: closing INC12345 as resolved at 2025-11-03T14:51:05Z. Monitoring for 1h post-close.

andrew: thumbs up. Postmortem draft link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/XXX-123 (will update).

sara: adding follow-ups: metric quota for cardinality, canary exporter config rollouts, add exporter mem alerts.

mike: adding an ops playbook task: implement temporary metric proxy to replay cached metrics when scrapes fail.

andrew: thanks — good incident run. :thumbsup:
